signals.raise: USD 1bn minority stake sale at USD 8.65bn valuation (Dec 2025; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraken_Technologies)

name: Kraken Technologies
desc: Builds the Kraken operating platform that energy and water utilities use to run billing, customer service and smart-grid flexibility.
ownership: private: majority-owned by Octopus Energy Group
capacity_detail: Minority stake sold for USD 1bn in December 2025, valuing Kraken at USD 8.65bn
markets: Licensed by about 40 utilities in 27 countries, including UK, US, Europe, Australia and Japan; over 70 million accounts contracted
rationale: Planned demerger from Octopus makes a standalone global B2B brand; F1 hospitality reaches utility executives across its 27-country client base.

name: Topsoe
desc: Danish supplier of catalysts, process technology and solid oxide electrolysers for clean fuels, ammonia and hydrogen.
markets: Customers worldwide in refining, chemicals, aviation, marine, metals, cement and power; offices across Americas, Europe, Middle East and Asia
rationale: Positions as decarbonisation technology leader for aviation and heavy industry; F1's sustainable-fuel push from 2026 gives a direct technical story.

name: Enercon
desc: German manufacturer of gearless onshore wind turbines, installed in more than 50 countries, owned by the Aloys Wobben Foundation.
markets: Sales offices in 25 countries; turbines installed in more than 50 countries; production in Germany, Poland, Portugal and Turkey
rationale: Competes with listed rivals Vestas and Siemens Gamesa for European and emerging-market orders; F1 offers B2B hospitality and an engineering-precision narrative.

name: Fronius International
desc: Austrian maker of solar inverters, welding systems and battery-charging technology with 36 subsidiaries worldwide.
markets: 36 international subsidiaries and sales partners in more than 60 countries across Europe, Americas, Asia and Australia
rationale: Inverter brand selling to installers and homeowners against SMA and Huawei; welding and charging lines also suit motorsport engineering storytelling.

name: St1
desc: Nordic fuel retailer and refiner producing renewable HVO diesel, waste-based ethanol and liquefied biogas for transport.
markets: Fuel stations and energy operations in Finland, Sweden, Norway and the United Kingdom
rationale: Consumer-facing fuel brand pushing renewable fuels; F1's 100% sustainable fuel era gives a credible link for Nordic and UK forecourt marketing.

name: Vaillant Group
desc: Family-owned German maker of heat pumps, boilers and cooling systems sold in more than 60 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue about EUR 3.3bn (Wikipedia infobox as of June 2026)
markets: Brands present in more than 60 countries; production in five European countries, Turkey and China
rationale: Heat-pump growth depends on consumer brand trust in Europe; F1's large German and UK audiences suit a household-name decarbonisation message.

sponsorships: Jersey sponsor TBV Lemgo handball; Swiss Cup football sponsor (2010)
name: Stiebel Eltron
desc: German family-owned manufacturer of heat pumps, ventilation and hot-water appliances with subsidiaries in Europe, Asia and the US.
ownership: family-owned: Stiebel family foundation and Frank Stiebel
markets: Subsidiaries in ten European countries, China, Japan, Thailand and the United States; sales representatives in 20 countries
rationale: Already uses sports sponsorship for brand building; heat-pump makers need consumer awareness in Germany and UK, both core F1 markets.

signals.raise: USD 240M equity round led by NantWorks (Mar 2026; https://www.fusionenergybase.com/articles/shine-technologies-240-million-funding-round)

name: SHINE Technologies
desc: Uses fusion neutron technology to produce medical isotopes and test materials, aiming at fuel recycling and fusion power.
capacity_detail: Raised more than USD 1bn in total, including USD 240M equity round led by NantWorks (2026)
markets: United States isotope, defence and aerospace testing customers; office and planned isotope production in Veendam, Netherlands
rationale: Revenue-generating fusion company seeking investor and talent visibility; F1 engineering audience suits its pragmatic path-to-fusion story.

name: CORE POWER
desc: Develops floating nuclear power plants and marine reactor applications for ports, shipping and coastal industry.
capacity_detail: USD 219M raised over 8 rounds, latest USD 24M (Oct 2025), per New Market Pitch funding ranking
markets: UK-based with partners in Japan shipbuilding and US ports, including a Port of Corpus Christi agreement
rationale: Needs maritime and port-industry credibility worldwide; F1 hospitality in Singapore, Japan and US races reaches shipowners and port authorities.

name: Nexeon
desc: British developer and manufacturer of silicon-based anode materials that raise lithium-ion battery energy density.
capacity_detail: USD 365M raised in total, latest USD 133M (Aug 2026), per New Market Pitch funding ranking
markets: Battery and automotive customers in Europe and Asia; investors include Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures
rationale: Supplies carmakers' battery chains; F1 hybrid-power platform lets it court automotive engineering buyers and highlight British advanced materials.

name: Nyobolt
desc: Cambridge company developing ultra-fast charging battery systems for data centres, robots and autonomous vehicles.
capacity_detail: USD 180M raised in total, latest USD 60M Series C (May 2026), per New Market Pitch funding ranking
markets: AI data centre power, autonomous mobile robots, humanoids and autonomous vehicles in UK, US and other markets
rationale: Fast-charging performance story maps naturally onto motorsport; F1 audience includes automotive and robotics engineers it wants as customers.

signals.raise: Series B+ over CNY 1bn, about USD 140M (Jun 2026; https://newmarketpitch.com/blogs/news/grid-battery-storage-top-startups-fundraising)

name: Dalian Rongke Power
desc: Chinese manufacturer of vanadium redox flow battery systems for long-duration grid energy storage projects.
capacity_detail: USD 171M raised in total incl. Series B+ over CNY 1bn (Jun 2026), per New Market Pitch grid storage ranking
markets: Grid-scale long-duration storage projects mainly in China
rationale: Chinese storage makers are expanding abroad; F1 Shanghai and global races could build international recognition for flow batteries.

name: China Storage Guoneng
desc: Chinese developer of compressed-air energy storage technology and power plants for grid-scale long-duration storage.
capacity_detail: USD 242M raised in total, latest USD 143M (May 2023), per New Market Pitch funding ranking
markets: Grid storage plants in China
rationale: Weak fit today; F1 Shanghai could support any future export push, but its customers are mainly Chinese grid operators.

name: WeLion New Energy
desc: Chinese manufacturer of hybrid solid-state lithium batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage.
capacity_detail: At least USD 280M raised (excludes undisclosed rounds incl. 2025 Series D+), per New Market Pitch solid-state ranking
markets: Chinese electric-vehicle makers and energy-storage customers
rationale: Solid-state batteries are a headline EV technology; F1 Shanghai and global broadcasts could raise its profile with international carmakers.

name: Blue Current
desc: US developer of solid-state silicon battery cells for electric vehicles, backed by Koch and Amazon.
capacity_detail: USD 150M+ raised, latest USD 81M Series D (Sep 2025), per New Market Pitch funding ranking
markets: Electric-vehicle and battery customers in the United States
rationale: Pre-scale battery maker courting carmakers; F1's hybrid era and US races reach automotive decision-makers, though budget is modest.

name: Element Energy
desc: US company building battery management and energy-storage systems for grid and commercial customers.
capacity_detail: USD 170M raised in total, latest USD 97M (Nov 2025), per New Market Pitch funding ranking
markets: Grid and commercial energy-storage projects in the United States
rationale: Battery-reuse story fits F1's sustainability messaging; US races could reach utility and automotive partners.

name: Urenco
desc: Enriches uranium for nuclear power station fuel at plants in the UK, Germany, the Netherlands and the US.
ownership: state-owned: UK Government Investments 33.3%, Dutch state 33.3%; E.ON and RWE 16.5% each
markets: Enrichment plants in Germany, Netherlands, UK and US supplying nuclear utilities across Europe, Americas and Asia
rationale: Nuclear fuel demand is rising with SMRs and data centres; F1 hospitality reaches global utility buyers, though B2B-only and state-owned.

name: Snowy Hydro
desc: Australian government-owned generator running the Snowy Mountains hydro scheme and the Red Energy and Lumo Energy retailers.
markets: Electricity generation in New South Wales and Victoria and retail customers across eastern Australia
rationale: Red Energy retail brand competes for Australian households; the Melbourne Grand Prix offers a high-profile domestic platform for Snowy 2.0's renewable story.

name: Hydro Tasmania
desc: Tasmanian government-owned hydropower generator that also owns the Momentum Energy electricity retailer in mainland Australia.
markets: Hydropower in Tasmania; retail electricity in mainland Australia through Momentum Energy
rationale: Momentum Energy competes for retail customers in Victoria, home of the Australian Grand Prix; weak fit for a global series.

name: BC Hydro
desc: Crown corporation generating mostly hydroelectric power and serving more than four million customers in British Columbia.
markets: Electricity generation and supply across British Columbia, Canada
rationale: Monopoly provincial utility with little commercial need for global sponsorship; included for completeness given scale and clean-power profile.

name: Copersucar
desc: Brazilian producer-owned marketer of sugar and ethanol, selling 21 billion litres of ethanol in Brazil and the US.
ownership: co-operative: owned by producer mills through holding Produpar
capacity_detail: Revenue BRL 65.8bn in the 2025/26 crop year
markets: Brazil and United States ethanol markets via Eco-Energy; global sugar trading through Alvean
rationale: Positions ethanol as a decarbonisation fuel for transport and shipping; F1's sustainable-fuel era and São Paulo Grand Prix fit its narrative.

name: IBC Solar
desc: German supplier of complete photovoltaic and storage systems and developer of solar parks in over 30 countries.
markets: Present in more than 30 countries, mainly Europe, with solar park projects abroad
rationale: Sells through installer networks in Germany and Europe; modest budget makes a team supplier or regional race deal more realistic.

name: Targray
desc: Canadian supplier of solar manufacturing materials, lithium-ion battery materials and traded biodiesel across North America, Europe and Asia.
markets: Offices and terminals in Canada, US, Czech Republic, UAE, Belgium, Switzerland, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and India
rationale: Supplies battery and solar manufacturers worldwide; Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal offers a home-market B2B hospitality platform.

name: Glen Dimplex
desc: Irish family-owned maker of electric heating, cooling and domestic appliances with operations across Europe, North America and Asia.
markets: Manufacturing in Ireland, UK and China; branches in North America, Germany, Netherlands, Japan, Poland, Belgium, France, Australia, Scandinavia
rationale: Has used football shirt sponsorship before; electrification of home heating is a consumer message suited to UK and European F1 audiences.

sponsorships: Top sponsor of SV Werder Bremen (Bundesliga); name sponsor EWE Baskets Oldenburg and EWE Arena
name: EWE
industry: regional energy, grid and telecoms utility
desc: German municipally controlled utility running power, gas and telecom networks in north-west Germany and developing onshore wind.
markets: Ems-Weser-Elbe region, Bremen, Brandenburg and Rügen in Germany
rationale: Already a Bundesliga top sponsor, so sports budgets exist; however its customer base is regional Germany, limiting global F1 value.

name: Danfoss
industry: drives, heat pumps and climate solutions
desc: Danish foundation-owned engineering group making drives, heat pumps, heating controls and hydraulic power components with 95 factories worldwide.
ownership: family-owned: Bitten and Mads Clausen Foundation
markets: 95 production sites worldwide including Denmark, Germany, United States and China; China is a major market
rationale: Markets electrification and energy efficiency to industrial buyers worldwide; F1 hybrid engineering and hospitality suit its B2B decarbonisation brand.

name: ENUSA
desc: Spanish state-owned company supplying enriched uranium and nuclear fuel assemblies to Spanish and foreign nuclear power plants.
markets: Nuclear power plants in Spain and abroad
rationale: State-owned B2B fuel supplier with little consumer-brand need; included because it passes the capacity test, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Looop
desc: Japanese electricity retailer selling Looop Denki power plans and developing, installing and maintaining solar power systems.
capacity_detail: Revenue JPY 45,591m (non-consolidated) in year to March 2024
markets: Electricity retail and solar projects in Japan
rationale: Consumer power retailer competing for Japanese households; the Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka offers a domestic brand-building platform.

sponsorships: Official Bioethanol Partner of NASCAR (2026); Richard Childress Racing collaboration
name: POET
desc: US bioethanol producer operating 35 bioprocessing facilities with 3.1 billion gallons of annual ethanol capacity in the Midwest.
capacity_detail: Official Bioethanol Partner of NASCAR (2026), with collaboration with Richard Childress Racing
markets: Bioethanol production across rural US Midwest; fuel blending markets in the United States
rationale: Already spends on NASCAR to promote bioethanol; F1's sustainable-fuel rules and US races at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas extend that story.

name: Messer Group
desc: Family-owned German industrial gases company supplying hydrogen and decarbonisation services across Europe, Asia and the Americas.
ownership: family-owned: founding family and Dr. Hans Messer Stiftung
markets: Operations in Europe, Asia, North and South America; competence centres in Germany, Austria, Hungary and China
rationale: Competes with listed Linde and Air Liquide for industrial customers; F1 hospitality and technical partnership could raise its profile in hydrogen.

name: Tereos
desc: French farmer co-operative producing sugar, starch and bioethanol in 44 factories across nine countries.
markets: Factories in France, Belgium, Brazil, India, Indonesia, Kenya and Tanzania among nine countries
rationale: Bioethanol producer that could tie its renewable-fuel output to F1's sustainable fuel era, though its core brand is sugar.
